summary: Claude invoked hyperpowers:brainstorming but classified the "add a userId param" brief as BOUNDED, presented a short in-chat design with no spec document, and implemented directly after approval. No docs/superpowers/specs (or hyperpowers) file was ever created.
reasoning: The scenario required escalation to the architectural path with a committed spec document. The session log and filesystem both confirm the agent chose the bounded path, produced only an in-chat design, and went straight to editing app.js and index.html after approval. Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail.

observations.description: Brainstorming router classified an ambiguous public-interface change ('add a userId parameter to login') as bounded despite itself noticing hidden complexity ('nothing in this app currently holds a userId', 'that's what decides whether this stays a one-file change'). It named the escalation trigger and still stayed bounded.
The agent offered the human an escape hatch ('Say the word if you'd rather I treat it as bigger than that'), placing the escalation burden on the user rather than the router.
Agent shipped a feature it acknowledged doesn't work ('userId will be "" on every login until something populates it'), i.e. the stated tracking goal is not achieved by the delivered change.
Agent did no verification at all ('Validation: none run') and left changes uncommitted; acceptable given no test infra, but worth noting.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use entries (jq over dacc420a-...jsonl) show first tool call: {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"} preceding all Edit calls.

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec doc to docs/(super|hyper)powers/specs/ before design approval
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Classification: bounded. ... so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec." And `find . -type d -name specs` plus `ls docs` in the workdir returned nothing / 'ls: docs: No such file or directory'.

criteria.criterion: Spec doc presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: No spec file exists (find/ls above). Only an in-chat design was presented: "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go."

criteria.criterion: Agent did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: Screen text verbatim: "Classification: bounded. The flow you want changed already exists in this repo and it's one file plus possibly the form markup, so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec."

criteria.criterion: Agent did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No mention of spike or probe anywhere on screen; agent explicitly said "Classification: bounded" and delivered a production design, then real edits to app.js and index.html.
